B_access_pricing.mcp_access_cost_details: The official hosted-server page describes availability to Tableau Cloud customers on any SKU, but does not state a separate MCP charge. MartechDB reports no extra charge; this is third-party evidence.
B_access_pricing.linked_software_cost: NOT FOUND in accessible official pricing evidence; the official pricing page returned HTTP 403.
B_access_pricing.pricing_model_details: Tableau Cloud SKU and feature entitlements gate some tools; Tableau+ is required for Pulse Insight Briefs and Tableau Knowledge, while Data Management is needed for the full Metadata API surface. Official docs do not establish an MCP-specific fee.
B_access_pricing.other_access_restrictions: Hosted service is for Tableau Cloud, not Tableau Server. Access requires OAuth 2.1 sign-in and is subject to user permissions and site SKU entitlements. Site administrators cannot disable the hosted service itself but can exclude tool groups through site settings.
B_access_pricing.restrictions_controlled_by: Vendor controls hosted availability and pod routing; organization/site administrators control tool group exclusions and user roles; Tableau entitlements and the signed-in user's permissions also constrain use.

C_capabilities.description_what_how: The official hosted documentation lists tools for data sources, workbooks, views, flows, Pulse, administration, knowledge context, and data apps. It says the hosted service exposes the full tool catalog, subject to SKU entitlements and user permissions. The current official Web tool-name source names 55 tools, more than the 40 rows in the docs table (including a repeated delete-content row).
C_capabilities.post_interaction_context_structure: The docs describe structured results for some tools, such as list-datasources returning {data, totalAvailable}; general result and error schemas were not available in the inspected materials.

C_capabilities.post_interaction_context_structure: Prompt content orchestrates multiple tools; the docs describe inform and apply workflows for stale content, jobs, extract schedules, and user licenses.

D_server_side_logic.additional_logic: 1. Tool mix: documented tools include reads and mutating operations (flow run/cancel, content deletion, schedule update, user-role update, knowledge writes, workbook/data source publishing in source names). The reviewed docs do not show readOnlyHint, destructiveHint, idempotentHint, or openWorldHint annotations. 2. Server-enforced confirmation: docs describe preview and confirmation for flow mutations and two-phase content deletion; update schedule and user role are confirm-gated. Whether confirmation tokens are enforced in the hosted build is not verified from handlers. 3. Hosted OAuth authenticates each user as their Tableau Cloud identity; permissions and site roles apply. Admin tools require administrator role; admin tools are controlled by ADMIN_TOOLS_ENABLED in self-host configuration. OAuth metadata does not advertise DCR endpoint or token lifetime. 4. Hosted endpoint is global and pod-aware; hosted service is Cloud-only. Site admins cannot disable the service but can set EXCLUDE_TOOLS. Self-hosted configuration supports include/exclude tool names/groups and result caps. 5. Hosted docs say calls are proxied using the user's access token and Tableau data is not stored by the service. No field-level masking or PII exclusion is stated. 6. Hosted rate limits/call quotas/costs are not found. Self-hosted docs describe configurable result caps; docs describe list-datasources pages up to 1,000 and other tool limits. 7. Hosted validation/correction details are not found. Self-host docs describe parameter limits and error handling, but handler code was unavailable locally. 8. Hosted OAuth sign-ins and tool calls are logged through standard activity/audit pipelines. Self-host docs describe product telemetry and configurable telemetry behavior, but this cannot be attributed to the hosted deployment. 9. No feedback/rating/survey action appears in the official tool-name source. Hosted documentation does not show upsell messages. 10. Docs state pre-built skills are coming soon; no server-delivered skills were established. Workflow prompts and resources can guide agent behavior; tool descriptions include preview/confirmation guidance. 11. No evidence found that past agent behavior changes future hosted outputs or available tools. 12. Pod-aware routing delegates requests to the correct Cloud pod; one global URL is documented. No nested MCP sub-server was found. 13. No universal raw API, SQL, or script execution tool found in the official Web tool-name list.

F_documentation.implementation_hints_not_enforced: Docs instruct clients to use OAuth and explain permission requirements. Tool descriptions recommend preview/confirmation for selected mutations. Hosted handler enforcement was not verified because the local code copy was missing. Quote: "The MCP server then makes Tableau REST API calls as that user, so every existing per-user permission and access control is enforced automatically."
F_documentation.governance_promises: Hosted docs state: "The hosted service does not store your Tableau data." They also state OAuth sign-ins and tool calls are logged through standard activity and audit pipelines, and per-user permissions are respected. No hosted retention period or AI training terms were found in the captured pages.
F_documentation.promises_to_user: The service is managed, available on every Tableau Cloud pod, and continuously updated without a client-side upgrade. It is available to Tableau Cloud customers on any SKU, with some tools gated by entitlements.
F_documentation.comparison_with_server_logic: The endpoint OAuth challenge and metadata substantiate authentication. Hosted docs describe per-user authorization, audit logging, and no storage, but the implementation was not inspected locally; these remain documented promises rather than independently verified server-side logic. The global endpoint and OAuth metadata support the documented connection model.

contradictions: Official intro table contains 39 unique tool names (40 rows with delete-content repeated), while the official repository's current Web tool-name file names 55 tools. The source file includes additional names such as confirm-delete-content, publish-datasource, move-workbook, and token-management tools; the hosted docs say the full catalog is available, so the docs table appears incomplete or out of sync.

OAuth scope metadata advertises workbook create/update, file upload, project read, knowledge write, and other capabilities, while the intro tool table omits several matching current code names. The scope list is broader than the docs table and does not establish that every scope maps to a currently enabled tool.
Prepared code/GITHUB_COMMITS.txt records an incomplete GitHub read and no local repository snapshot, so the repository's exact commit and handler behavior could not be pinned or examined.
observations_for_research: A single global endpoint routes to customer-specific Cloud pods after authentication; user identity and existing Tableau permissions form the documented authorization context.
The hosted page describes service-level tool-group exclusion by site administrators while explicitly stating the hosted service itself cannot be disabled by those administrators.
The documentation tool table and the official repository's Web tool-name file are materially out of sync, so the published table alone understates the public source's named surface.
OAuth scopes expose operation families and permissions that are not apparent from the incomplete docs tool table.
